title: Compact direct images needed by the generic argument
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated finite-type morphism between
finite-type schemes over a field of characteristic different from
$\ell$. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathbf F_\ell)$, its
compact direct image
$Rf_!K$ is bounded constructible. For every morphism $v:S'\to S$ with Noetherian $S'$,
the compact direct-image exchange
$v^*Rf_!K\to Rf'_!v_X^*K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ (with $\ell$ prime). The field spectrum is Noetherian: its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem gives that $X$ and $S$ are Noetherian. In particular $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: a finite cover by Noetherian affines makes its topological space Noetherian, so every open, including an intersection of two affine opens, is quasi-compact. Apply Nagata to the separated finite-type $f$ and obtain a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$. By the definition of compactification, $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ is proper. Since proper morphisms are finite type, finite-type Noetherian permanence applied to $p$ first gives that $\overline X$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact. Clause (e) of the cited permanence lemma makes the composite of $p$ with the structure morphism of $S$ locally of finite type. Its target is the affine one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose whole inverse image is the quasi-compact $\overline X$; thus this composite is quasi-compact and consequently finite type over the same field. The ordinary small-etale compact-support definition identifies $Rf_!K$ with $Rp_*j_!K$.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences; Nagata: Stacks Tag 0F41, flat.tex theorem-nagata; Noetherian permanence: Tag 01T6

proof.text: Choose $a\le b$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Extension by zero along $j$ is exact by the cited extension-by-zero proposition. Thus the exact-functor cohomology comparison gives $\mathcal H^q(j_!K)\cong j_!\mathcal H^q(K)$. For $q\in[a,b]$, each right hand side is constructible by the extension-by-zero constructibility lemma, applied with ambient scheme $\overline X$, which is finite type over the field. For the other $q$ it is zero, since an additive functor sends zero to zero. Therefore $j_!K$ is bounded constructible on $\overline X$, by the definition of that category.

source.place: Proof, extension-by-zero sentence; Stacks Tag 03S6, etale-cohomology.tex lemma-shriek-base-change

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ is finite and killed by $\ell$; $\ell$ is invertible on every scheme over the given field because its characteristic differs from $\ell$. Thus these are the finite coefficients required by the proper bounded-constructibility lemma. Apply that lemma to $p:\overline X\to S$ and the bounded constructible complex $j_!K$ from step 2. Both schemes are finite type over the field by step 1 and $p$ is proper. It follows that $Rp_*j_!K$, and hence $Rf_!K$, belongs to $D^b_c(S,A)$.

Let $v:S\prime\to S$ be any of the stated morphisms. Using the base-change compactification definition, form $\overline X\prime=\overline X\times_S S\prime$, with $p\prime:\overline X\prime\to S\prime$, $w:\overline X\prime\to\overline X$, and $j\prime:X\prime=X\times_S S\prime\hookrightarrow\overline X\prime$. The compactification-base-change lemma says that $(j\prime,p\prime)$ is a compactification of $f\prime$. In particular $p\prime$ is proper and finite type; since $S\prime$ is Noetherian, $\overline X\prime$ is Noetherian by finite-type Noetherian permanence. The open subscheme $X\prime$ is locally Noetherian, and its underlying open subset of the Noetherian topological space $\overline X\prime$ is quasi-compact, so $X\prime$ is also Noetherian. The ordinary compact-support definition is consequently applicable to this compactification too. The extension-by-zero base-change proposition, applied to the square for $j$ and $w$, supplies the isomorphism $w^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j\prime_!v_X^{-1}K$ for complexes. This step requires no finite-type-over-the-original-field hypothesis on $S\prime$.

source.place: Proof, base-changed compactification and extension-by-zero comparison; Stacks Tag 03S6

proof.text: The complex $j_!K$ is bounded below and all its cohomology is killed by $\ell$, hence torsion. Apply bounded-below proper base change to the Cartesian square for $p$ and $v$ to obtain an isomorphism $v^{-1}Rp_*(j_!K)\to Rp\prime_*w^{-1}(j_!K)$ after forgetting coefficients. The exchange-forget-coefficients lemma identifies this specified abelian exchange with the underlying exchange in $A$-module derived categories and reflects its invertibility. Hence the displayed proper exchange is an isomorphism in $D^+(S\prime_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ itself. This uses only properness of $p$, bounded-below torsion cohomology of $j_!K$, and the Cartesian square; it does not require $S\prime$ to have finite type over a field.

source.place: Proof, proper comparison; Stacks Tag 095T, etale-cohomology.tex theorem-proper-base-change, with bounded-below extension supplied by cited theorem

proof.text: For the constant ring $A$, inverse image equals module pullback $u^*$ and is exact, by inverse-image exactness. Thus the notation $v^*,v_X^*$ agrees with $v^{-1},v_X^{-1}$. In the compact-support exchange definition, the inverse image acting on $j_!K$ is along the ambient projection $w:\overline X\prime\to\overline X$ (the displayed $g^{-1}j_!K$ there is a typing error: its $g$ has target $S$, not $\overline X$). With this explicitly typed extension-zero comparison, its representative using $(j,p)$ and its base change is precisely the composite $v^{-1}Rp_*j_!K\to Rp\prime_*w^{-1}j_!K\to Rp\prime_*j\prime_!v_X^{-1}K$. The first arrow is the isomorphism from step 5. The second is the image under $Rp\prime_*$ of the isomorphism from step 4, so its inverse is the image of the inverse of that isomorphism. The compact-support identifications identify the endpoints with $v^*Rf_!K$ and $Rf\prime_!v_X^*K$. The inverse of the composite is the composite of these two inverses in reverse order. This proves the asserted invertibility of the specified compact-support exchange.
